priceSnapshot.source: OKX public API /market/candles for BTC-USDT, read at 12:47 COT from inside a browser tab on the okx.com origin, which sidesteps the run proxy entirely. Four granularities read within ninety seconds of each other agree: the in-progress 15m bar opening 2026-08-22T17:45Z prints 77,275.9, the in-progress 1H bar opening 17:00Z prints 77,275.9, and the in-progress UTC daily bar opening 00:00Z prints the same. FRESHNESS GUARD APPLIED AND PASSED THIS TIME: the newest 15m stamp is 17:45Z against a wall clock of 17:47Z, so the series is genuinely current rather than a cached replay. changePct is measured against the settled 1H close exactly twenty-four bars back, the 2026-08-21T17:00Z bar at 77,393.1: 77,275.9 / 77,393.1 - 1 = -0.15 percent.
priceSnapshot.note: Against the morning report's 77,121.9 spot is UP 154.0 points, or 0.20 percent, in five hours and forty-nine minutes. The number is almost the whole story: this has been a coil, not a trend. Since the morning snapshot at 11:45Z the entire range is 76,882.0 to 77,573.4 - 691.4 points, or 1.13 of a single hourly ATR across six hours of tape. Neither gate the morning report set was reached on a close. The 16:00Z hour ran to 77,573.4, clearing the 77,519.1 add line on the wick, and then settled back at 77,294.7. The reduce line at 76,515.0 was never approached: the lowest print of the whole session is 76,882.0, some 367 points above it. sessionRange is measured from the 11:45Z 15m bar onward, i.e. since the morning portfolio snapshot at 06:45 COT.

reduceIf.confirmation: A settled 1H close below $76,515.0 - unchanged for the third session running, and the level this desk has now named three times without ever seeing it break. It was traded to exactly at 05:00Z and missed by 14.9 points at 10:00Z, and on both occasions the hour closed hundreds of points higher. Spot sits 760.9 points above the line, which is 1.24 hourly ATRs, so it is no longer within casual reach of one ordinary hour. The trigger remains a settled CLOSE, not a wick. A close through it says the bid that absorbed two flushes is finally gone, and the next verified shelf is 76,222.2.

addIf.confirmation: A settled 1H close above $77,573.4 - the high of this session and 315.1 points above the 1H EMA20 at 77,258.32. This RAISES the morning gate from 77,519.1 by 54.3 points, and the reason is that 77,519.1 has already been tested and rejected: the 16:00Z hour ran through it to 77,573.4 and then closed 278.7 points back below. A gate that has been wicked and rejected is no longer a gate. The honest replacement is the price that did the rejecting. A settled close above it clears the only lower high the tape has made since 05:00Z and turns this coil into a continuation.

decisionBox.changed: Stance stays ADD and a third, smaller tranche goes in, the add gate moves up from 77,519.1 to 77,573.4, and the reduce line stays at 76,515.0 for the third session. Three things earned the tranche rather than a hold. Price has RECLAIMED the 1H EMA20 it lost this morning - it was 189.4 points beneath it at 06:58 COT and is 17.6 points above it now. The 1H MACD histogram has halved its deficit, from -305.28 to -165.16, on a higher low in price. And Farside published the 21 August row since the morning run: +307.5m, which extends the verified inflow streak from four days to five. Against that, the 4H RSI at 79.93 and the UTC daily RSI at 81.00 are still stretched and the heaviest liquidation magnets on the map sit 2,900 points BELOW spot, which is why this is 20 USDT and not 40.

liquidation.note: The nearest band of any weight above spot, 1,885.1 points up. Tooltip-read directly off the CoinGlass Model-3 heatmap at 398.19K of liquidation leverage against a colour-scale maximum of 1.35M, so it is a real shelf but a thin one. It is also the only thing between spot and the 78,832.2 daily high, which is why a squeeze through the add gate has comparatively little fuel behind it.

First band below spot, 1,167.4 points down, tooltip-read at 314.35K. It sits between the 76,222.2 invalidation and the 76,515.0 reduce line, which means the map agrees with the chart about where the next real test lives.

587.45K of liquidation leverage - the heaviest single band within 1,500 points of spot on either side, and nearly half again the size of anything above. If 76,515.0 goes on a close, this is the price the tape reaches for next.

354.30K, tooltip-read. It lines up almost exactly with the 75,611.2 shelf that has been in this report's support list since the 20 August impulse, so chart and heatmap are pointing at the same air pocket.

1.13M of liquidation leverage - the single brightest band anywhere on the visible 48-hour map, and 83 percent of the colour-scale maximum. It sits 2,897.2 points below spot. This is the magnet that defines the downside risk in this tape: it is not close, but nothing between here and there is heavy enough to stop a flush that gets going.

1.11M, 407 points beneath the brightest band. The two together form one continuous 73,970 to 74,380 shelf holding more leverage than everything above spot combined - the residue of the leverage that was built on the way up from 68,000 on 20 August.
380.47K, the last readable band before the map runs out of useful resolution. Included for scale rather than as a live level: it is 6.25 percent below spot.

liquidityMagnet.source: CoinGlass Liquidation Heatmap Model 3, Binance BTC/USDT perpetual, 48-hour window, read in the browser with per-band tooltips rather than from colour alone. Header aggregates from the same page. OKX free endpoints were tried first and both failed the freshness guard - see macro.liquidations.note.
liquidityMagnet.note: The pull is DOWN and it is not close. Above spot the heaviest readable band is 398.19K at 79,161. Below spot there are 1.13M at 74,378.75 and 1.11M at 73,971.75, plus 587.45K at 75,803.25. That is roughly 6.2 times more forced-liquidation fuel below than above within the readable range. This does not forecast direction - it says which way an accident travels further if one starts, and it is the reason this session added 20 USDT rather than 40.

atr.source: Computed in-browser from the last 300 OKX 1H BTC-USDT bars using Wilder true range (max of high-low, absolute high-minus-previous-close, absolute low-minus-previous-close), seeded on the first 14 true ranges and smoothed forward across the whole series. 613.04 against 718.52 at the morning run and 786.0 at midnight: the tape has now contracted for two consecutive sessions, a 22 percent drop in hourly range since midnight. pct = 613.04 / 77,275.9 = 0.79 percent.

timeframes.structure: Six hours of overlapping bars between 76,882.0 and 77,573.4 with no expansion. Spot is above the EMA20 and the EMA100 and 9.8 points above the EMA50, so the three fast averages have compressed into a 156-point band around price - the textbook shape of a coil rather than a trend.

The single most important change of the session: price has reclaimed the 1H EMA20. At 06:58 COT spot was 189.4 points below it; it is 17.6 points above it now. The MACD line is still beneath its signal but the histogram has contracted from -305.28 to -165.16 while price made a HIGHER low (76,529.9 at 10:00Z, 76,882.0 at 15:00Z). RSI has drifted from 51.53 to 53.27. Momentum is decompressing, not reversing.

Price is above all four EMAs and 3,084.7 points above the EMA20, so the trend is intact and extended. But the MACD histogram has crossed to -16.21 - the first negative 4H histogram since the 20 August impulse began, and the line is now 16.21 beneath its signal. That is a bearish cross by the narrowest possible margin. RSI at 79.93 has slipped just under the 80 line from 80.45 this morning.

Read on the 1Dutc bar so the day aligns with the calendar date this report is stamped with - note the morning run used OKX's default 1D, which opens at 16:00Z on a UTC+8 clock, so the two RSI figures are not directly comparable. Today's UTC session opened 78,338.1, ran to 78,832.2, flushed to 76,515.0 and sits 77,275.9, an inside-out day that is 1,062.2 points below yesterday's close. Price is above all four daily EMAs, including the EMA200 at 71,730.96 by 7.7 percent. RSI 81.00 is deeply overbought and the MACD histogram at 1,579.5 is the widest of the whole advance.

etfFlows.note: THIS CHANGED SINCE THE MORNING RUN. Farside published the 21 August row while this session was between reports: IBIT +239.3m, total +307.5m. The morning report could only see dashes there and counted four days. The verified streak is now FIVE consecutive settled inflow days - 17 Aug +297.5m, 18 Aug +189.3m, 19 Aug +517.2m, 20 Aug +606.3m, 21 Aug +307.5m - totalling +1,917.8m, preceded by three negative days (12 Aug -61.1m, 13 Aug -131.1m, 14 Aug -56.2m). The shape is worth reading honestly: 21 August is HALF the size of 20 August, so the acceleration stopped even as the streak extended. Five days of genuine spot demand is still the strongest argument that this advance is flow-led rather than a leverage squeeze, and it is the main reason this run adds rather than trims. It is now the weekend, so no further flow data can arrive before Monday and this reading will be stale for the next two sessions.

liquidations.note: BOTH OKX free liquidation endpoints failed the freshness guard this run and were DISCARDED, so nothing here comes from them. The open-interest endpoint returned a snapshot stamped 03:06Z - fourteen hours and forty minutes stale - and returned the identical byte-for-byte payload on a cache-busted retry. The realized liquidation-orders endpoint was worse: every one of the 100 prints it returned was stamped 5 August 2026 at prices around 65,100, seventeen days and 12,000 points away from this tape. longsUsd and shortsUsd are therefore NULL rather than guessed. The browser fallback to CoinGlass worked and supplies the rest. openInterestUsd 137,420,898,839 is the CoinGlass cross-exchange aggregate from the page header, down 1.21 percent on 24 hours - it is NOT the OKX BTC-USDT-SWAP figure the morning runs use, so do not compare the two series directly. skew 0.96 is the header's 24-hour long/short liquidation split, 49.06 percent longs against 50.94 percent shorts, which is as close to balanced as this metric gets and a clean normalisation from the 1.78-to-1 long-side skew the morning run measured. Total 24-hour liquidations across the market: 1,227,935,404 USD, down 11.72 percent. Two OKX feeds that DID pass the guard, for context: funding on BTC-USDT-SWAP settled the 16:00Z period at exactly 0.0100 percent, the neutral baseline, so there is still no crowded-long premium in the perp; and the long/short account ratio stamped 13:00Z reads 1.07, down from 1.14 at 05:00Z and 1.50 yesterday - retail longs have genuinely de-crowded rather than doubled down.

calibration.rollingRecord: Three sessions today, three tranches, no gate ever fired on a close.
calibration.note: The morning report set reduce at 76,515.0 and add at 77,519.1 and NEITHER fired on a settled close. The reduce line was not approached at all - the session low of 76,882.0 is 367 points above it. The add line was wicked at 16:00Z to 77,573.4 and rejected on the close at 77,294.7, which is why this run raises the gate rather than pretending it was met. On the money: morning deployed 18.00 USDT into the spot core at 77,121.9 and spot is 77,275.9, so that tranche is up 0.20 percent, roughly 0.04 USDT. Midnight's 24.00 USDT at 77,599.2 is still down 0.42 percent. Net across today's two tranches the desk is fractionally underwater and the honest read is that both entries were early relative to the levels they named. What the morning got RIGHT was the reasoning: it said the twice-defended 76,515.0 shelf justified averaging rather than abandoning, and the shelf has now gone a third session without being tested. What it got wrong was the add gate - 77,519.1 was set inside the session's own high, so it was always likely to be wicked without being confirmed.
